test_title: PYST 20: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 26 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2
solution:
The correct answer is '**impetus**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The passage discusses the consequences of the food industry's growth on international trade and responsibilities.
 
• The appropriate noun should indicate a driving force that has led to an increase in trade.
 
• "**Impetus**" fits well as it denotes a driving force or incentive, which aligns with the context of the food industry's growth spurring international trade.
 
• Other options ("**energy**", "**assurance**", "**motivation**") do not fit the context of describing the driving factor behind increased trade.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The food industry in India accounts for about 26 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) and will be one of the major__ growth areas in the years ahead. This has given *__*impetus*__* to international trade but has also increased the responsibility to achieve the appropriate level of _____3______ in terms of sanitary and phytosanitary protection. Further, the Indian Food Safety and Standards Act of 2006, reflects a major shift in food laws and seeks to provide greater consumer protection by _________4_______ the safety and wholesomeness of food at all stages of the food chain. This changing scenario has widened the scope and ________5______ career options in this area.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Energy**: "Energy" refers to capacity for activity or work; it does not fit the context of a driving force for trade.
 
• **Assurance**: "Assurance" means a promise or confidence; it does not reflect the idea of a driving force behind trade.
 
• **Motivation**: "Motivation" means the reason or reasons for acting or behaving a certain way; while related, it does not fit as well as "impetus" in the context of trade development.
